title: Sage Accounting Pricing 2026 After the Discount Ends
summary: Sage Accounting pricing starts with a free tier and goes up to advanced plans.
body_markdown:
## Sage plan costs at realistic usage


You can count three inputs, and they decide what each plan costs:


- users
- invoices in your busiest month
- the month the introductory discount ends


Price those three against the plan limits and the monthly figure on the pricing page stops mattering.


Run the same sum for each of the three firms below. Take the monthly price of the cheapest plan whose invoice and user limits you stay inside.


Multiply the discounted rate by the months the discount runs, then the full rate by the months left in a 12-month year.


Add any add-on you can't do without. The gap between that total and twelve times the headline price is the part the pricing page doesn't show you.


### Solo freelancer: 1 user, 20 invoices a month


With one user and a low invoice count, the entry plan is most likely to fit. You're well inside the metered unit, invoices per month, even in a busy month.


If anything bites here, it's the discount ending, not a limit. From the month the introduction lapses, your bill's the same plan at a higher rate, so budget for the full-price figure from day one.


If the entry plan fits at full price, you can stay on it. If it only makes sense at the discounted rate, you've already found the point where it stops being cheap.


### Small team: 3 users, 100 invoices a month


Here the invoice count and the user count each push against a limit, and either can force you up a tier. Check the busiest month first.


A plan that fits for eleven months and fails in the twelfth still sets your price, because you pay the higher tier or an add-on for that month.


Then check whether extra users are a per-seat charge or a jump to another plan. The cheaper plan stops being cheaper at the point where its add-ons plus its rate exceed the next tier's flat rate, so work that comparison out explicitly.


> A plan that fits for eleven months and fails in the twelfth still sets your price, because you pay the higher tier or an add-on for that month.


### Growing firm: 5 users, 400 invoices a month


You're probably on a higher tier from the start at this size. That makes the introductory discount a smaller share of the year's cost, and the plan's limits matter more than the offer.


Count invoices at your peak, not your average, and price the next tier up as well. If your volume is still growing, the 12-month total at full price is the figure to plan around, because the discounted total describes a year you won't repeat.


Activepieces can run that count for you: a scheduled flow that tallies invoices and users, checks the renewal date and messages you before a cap is reached costs 1 credit per run however many steps it has, so the free plan's 1,000 monthly credits cover it many times over.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module, so the same flow gets dearer there with every step you add. It only works where Sage offers an integration or API route to those figures, and it has no bearing on what Sage charges.
